name: Dividend Arbitrage with Deep ITM Puts
summary: Buy shares and a deep ITM put just before the ex-dividend date so the share position is fully hedged while the dividend is collected, then exercise the put after the ex-date. Mostly historical.

legs.strike_rule: deep ITM, 0.90+ delta, with extrinsic value < the dividend per share

max_profit: dividend - put extrinsic - fees, per share; typically a few cents at best
max_loss: the put's extrinsic plus fees; the share risk is fully hedged by the deep ITM put
breakevens: n/a - the trade is a fixed small carry
when_to_use: Almost never. This was arbitraged away decades ago; modern option pricing embeds the dividend, so the put's extrinsic almost always exceeds the dividend. FLAGGED: a bad idea, included for completeness and so the system can recognize and reject it.
typical_dte: a few days - shortest expiry past the ex-date
entry_rules: Compute: expected_profit = dividend_per_share - put_extrinsic - all_fees. Require expected_profit >= $0.05 per share. In practice this condition is essentially never met.
Require the dividend to be declared, not estimated.
Require put delta >= 0.90 so the share hedge is near-complete.
Reject if the put's bid-ask spread exceeds the expected profit (it usually does).
management_rules: Hold only across the ex-date; there is nothing else to manage.
Do not let the hedge slip - a 0.90 delta put still leaves 10 deltas of share risk.
exit_rules: After the ex-date, EXERCISE the long put to sell the shares at the strike (this is the one case where exercising a long option is the intended exit), or close both legs at market if the combined price is better than the strike.
Never carry past the put's expiry.
assignment_risk: No short leg. The classic failure is that OTHER holders of the same put exercise, and the associated short-call/short-put open interest gets assigned - irrelevant here. The real risk is execution: paying more in spreads and fees than the dividend is worth.
buying_power: Full share cost plus the put premium for a few days.
liquidity_needs: Deep ITM puts are wide; this alone usually kills the trade.
common_mistakes: Believing the dividend is free money; not modeling that the put price already contains the dividend; ignoring that the share price drops by the dividend on the ex-date.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
